Overview

Awhile back I did a video series that went over programming a simple game engine from scratch. I picked it back up about a week ago, but I can't guarantee updates since I'm a pretty busy person (2 jobs, very little free time). I thought if any of you were interested you can have a look. This was an experiment by me and recording myself programming was so weird.. in the end I found it easier to take it slow as possible.

To facilitate the engine, I used a fairly new drawing library from Microsoft: Win2D which is an immediate mode drawing library. You can use any drawing library you want and adapt accordingly.

In the video series, I go over

  • Downloading the library with NuGet and importing it. Drawing simple geometric shapes onto the canvas.

  • Creating a Content Pipeline and loading Images into it.

  • Making basic scene items (objects), putting them inside a scene (aka Scene graph) and building a manager that manages all the scenes inside your game: A StoryBoard.

  • Creating the Game Loop which has a specific Updates Per Second and Frame Per Second.

  • Creating an Input Manager such that the mouse (or anything you like) can push its events on to it, which the manager pushes its current input down the StoryBoard model.

A spectre gazed over some painstakingly made schematics of a seafaring vessel.

The technical specifications and measurements taken from the Daylight's Retreat had been highly informative. Inside the beautiful form of the vessel there was simplicity and elegance, perfect for imitation. Never too precisely, never too exactly, for several parts of the Daylight's Retreat seem to have had some ties to her vanity.

The Spectra didn't care much for the aesthetics of the craft, they needed function. Neither did they need a large vessel for dominance, they needed a test case to show the world that the Spectra could take to sea.

So a simple craft had been designed, streamlined, smaller perhaps, but size was unnecessary after all. This was a statement, an explorer. It wasn't here to change the world, but it might just the same.

This was the [Edge of Dreams](http://ecx.images-amazon.com/images/I/51QzWleKh4L.jpg), the first caravel. The first foray of Sentenza into the heavy seas. An unarmed, light, small vessel to face the world. Nobody knew if it would survive its maiden voyage, in fact, some even doubt it will ever be built. The thing was that it didn't actually matter. Here was a proof of concept, a study of the vines.

So the Spectra will take to the seas, facing down the mighty storms. All this trouble, only to sate their curiosity.
